title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
comment: 28 pages. Single consolidated article, per the moderators' invitation (MOD-101633), merging submissions submit/7974478 and submit/7974538
summary: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed in hep-th/0404195 as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n. For the A_2^(2) family we give an exact Coulomb-gas dictionary to the dual Phi_{1,2}/Phi_{2,1} perturbations (that identification itself being classical, Zamolodchikov; Smirnov), whence the infinite hierarchy at all spins 6n+-1 follows by the Feigin-Frenkel affine-Toda theorem; our contribution is the certified dictionary, not a new all-spin construction. At c=1 the tower's defining charges are exactly quantum KdV at c_{1,4}=-25/2 -- the all-odd sector of the Freeman-Hornfeck-West family: the hierarchy embeds at every odd spin, equality verified through spin 15, all-spin multiplicity one open. We exclude or disfavor the named non-KdV candidates at the tested loci and identify the self-dual degeneracy as L(1,0). Through spin 11, the generic centralizer of I_3 is, for all three Z_2 x O(N) "cylindrical" families, one-dimensional at odd and zero at even spins, with Q(t)-symbolic charges at spins 7, 9, 11 and an explained fiber jump at N=-2. We certify the published 2004 low-spin formulas and record five corrections (one presumed). All-spin statements are made only where proved, finite-range otherwise. We close with a corank-character conjecture linking the rank deficiencies of the bilinear systems to characters of screening kernels.

title: Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
comment: 190 pages, 68 figures, 3 tables, 4 appendices; 85 plot files, jheppub-nosort.sty
summary: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations. Making use of the resulting exact Stokes automorphisms, nonperturbative solutions can be fully tested, from weak-to-strong 't Hooft coupling, as well as from large-to-small N, and for any complex-values of all parameters, by correctly implementing Stokes-transitions at the crossing of all possible Stokes-lines. Several analytical and numerical tests are carried through in diverse examples covering from matrix models through non-critical strings, which produce very sharp numerical matches fully validating our exact analytical expressions. Anti-eigenvalues or negative-tension D-branes are an absolutely essential part of the story in order to find such precise agreements.

title: Localizing the M-Theory Path Integral: Membrane Instantons
summary: We propose a formula for M2-instanton contributions to the M-theory path integral, incorporating quantum corrections to all orders in the Planck length. The M2-brane action is determined by relative equivariant localization, while an equivariant Dolbeault character computes the one-loop determinant. Continuous families of M2-branes are treated by equivariant localization on their moduli spaces. For M-theory backgrounds dual to ABJM theory, we compute single instanton contributions from linear holomorphic fillings to the sphere partition function and the topologically twisted index associated with supersymmetric $AdS_4$ black holes. Our results reproduce known field theory instanton coefficients and give new analytic predictions for mass and squashing deformations at all Chern-Simons levels. For the $V^{5,2}$ theory, we compute new instanton contributions and establish an exact relation between its partition function at special squashing and that of ABJM theory on the round three-sphere.

title: A Positive Metric on Four-Dimensional QFTs
summary: A natural metric on the space of four-dimensional quantum field theories was introduced by Jack and Osborn in classic work on the local renormalization group. In perturbation theory, the Jack-Osborn metric determines the flow of the $a$-anomaly, and positivity implies the $a$-theorem. We derive a non-perturbative generalization of the Jack-Osborn metric and show that it is non-negative by the averaged null energy condition (ANEC). Consequently, the ANEC implies the strong $a$-theorem, and provides the monotonic function along the flow. The method is based on spectral analysis of the three-point function $\langle \mathcal{O}_I \mathcal{E} \mathcal{O}_J\rangle$, where the $\mathcal{O}_I$ are relevant operators and $\mathcal{E}$ is the averaged null energy. This three-point function is decomposed under the spectrum of null rotations that fix the light ray, leading to a positivity condition at each impact parameter.

title: Generative diffusion models for lattice field theory
comment: 6 pages, contribution to the Proceedings of XQCD2026, Busan, Korea, 14-17 July 2026
summary: Generative diffusion models offer a new route to ensemble generation in lattice field theory. The backward, or denoising, process underlying these models is a stochastic process with a learned, time-dependent drift, which leads to a clear connection with stochastic quantisation. After reviewing this correspondence, I turn to theories with a sign problem. There the complex Boltzmann weight obstructs direct sampling, but complex Langevin dynamics can sometimes evade the sign problem by generating configurations on a complexified manifold, distributed according to a real and semi-positive distribution. This distribution is not known in closed form. I discuss how this distribution can be learned from complex Langevin data using score-based and, in particular, energy-based diffusion models. The latter give direct access to the unnormalised distribution itself, which can subsequently be used as the weight in a standard Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation. Results are shown for a simple quartic model with a complex action.

title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
summary: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.

title: Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in pulsar timing arrays
summary: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have found evidence for a gravitational wave background at nHz frequencies. Inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) likely contribute to at least part of the signal, but there may be additional cosmological sources from new physics in the early universe. Disentangling the two is complicated by the prohibitively slow modelling of SMBHB spectra based on realistic population models. Here we introduce binaryfog, a surrogate of up-to-date population models also used by the NANOGrav collaboration, that returns the statistical distribution of bent spectra $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ faster than direct computation. We use binaryfog to profile over the six astrophysical parameters in fits of four extensively discussed new-physics models: a dark sector phase transition, cosmic superstrings, inflationary gravitational waves, and domain walls. Compared to the widely adopted power-law description of the SMBHB background, the preference for a phase transition drops from $2.8σ$ to $1.5σ$. The other three models follow a similar pattern. We also recommend updated astrophysical priors based on galaxy surveys published since 2014, which for current PTA data still only give a marginal preference of $1.7σ$ for a phase transition. An interpretation of the signal in terms of SMBHBs alone favours binaries that merge within about $2\,$Gyr after their host galaxies have merged, requiring an efficient mechanism to overcome the final parsec of separation. If binaries need longer than about $6.5\,$Gyr to merge, the preference for a phase transition exceeds $3σ$ under our recommended updated prior set. binaryfog can help resolve these questions, as it allows users to study the impact of updated astrophysical priors and a realistic SMBHB population model on new-physics searches with PTAs.

title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
comment: 11 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Comments are welcome
summary: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.

title: JWST Observations of Starbursts: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in the NGC 253 Superwind
comment: 18 pages, 5 main figures, 4 appendix figures, submitted to ApJL
summary: We present the first spatially resolved study of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) evolution in the galactic superwind of the nearby (d~3.5Mpc) galaxy NGC 253. Using JWST MIRI and NIRCam, we image ~$\pm$2kpc along the galaxy minor axis, capturing both sides of the starburst-driven wind at ~0.05''-0.375'' (~0.85-6.4pc) resolution and providing one of the most detailed views of the wind to date. We target PAH emission at 3.3um, 7.7um, and 11.3um, revealing PAH-bright filamentary streamers along the limb-brightened edges of the outflow cones out to at least a deprojected distance r~0.5kpc, beyond which they likely become confused with the spiral arms. In the southwest (SW) and northeast (NE) streamers, PAH intensity declines faster than $r^{-2}$, suggesting either PAH destruction or a decrease in gas column density or dust-to-gas ratio rather than a response to declining illumination alone. Band ratios trace changes in PAH properties, with the 11.3/7.7um ratio increasing with distance in the SW and northwest (NW) streamers and 3.3/7.7um and 3.3/11.3um decreasing in the SW and NE streamers, indicating larger, more neutral PAHs farther from the starburst. Given the thermal and dynamical properties of the gas in the SW streamer, cool gas is expected to survive acceleration in the outflow and enable PAH shielding. Compared with those of the prototypical starburst M82, the NGC 253 band ratios indicate faster evolution in PAH size. Thus, the NGC 253 wind may represent an earlier stage of outflow evolution in which small PAHs are destroyed near the starburst within the first few Myr.

title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
summary: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_η(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-η_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. Its vacuum part is a dimension-four, CPT-even Lorentz-violating term of the Standard Model Extension with coefficient $(\cL)_{ii}=-η_0(m_i^2-m_1^2)/(2E_0^2)$, diagonal in the mass basis and fixed by the mass matrix, hence removable by a reparametrization. The matter-potential rescaling has dimension-five behaviour and is CPT-odd. For $f=1-η_0(E/E_0)^p$ the vacuum term behaves as a dimension $p+2$ operator and the matter term as $p+3$, so only $p=2$ gives a marginal vacuum operator; $p=0$ is absorbed into the measured mass splittings, and non-integer $p$ admits no local operator. For $η_0=0.02$ at $E_0=2.5$~GeV we find $|(\cL)_{33}|\simeq4\times10^{-24}$, comparable to present atmospheric bounds, whereas a Planck-suppressed deformation with $β_0=\mathcal{O}(1)$ gives $3.2\times10^{-58}$. At constant density it is equivalent to $L\to f(E)L$: mixing angles and the Dirac phase are unchanged, the CP asymmetry is reparametrized rather than generated, and the leading observable is a rescaling of $\dm_{31}$. At $1297$~km a re-fit of $\dm_{31}$ alone absorbs $23$~per cent of the squared probability difference, and a four-parameter re-fit absorbs $41.5$~per cent. No statistical analysis is performed; degeneracy means a distance in probability space, not a confidence interval.

title: Horizon kinematics and the fine structure induced by finite-energy Hawking radiation
summary: Hawking radiation can modify the horizon structure of a black hole through the loss of mass and global charges. Investigating this process through quantum tunneling, we develop a systematic strategy to reconstruct horizon displacements under finite-energy emission, even when their radii are not explicitly known. Inversion of the horizon condition allows to follow roots's displacements along sequences of static geometries. As a concrete realization, we consider a nonlinearly charged extension of the Bañados--Teitelboim--Zanelli (BTZ) family, whose horizon structure offers an ideal setup to explore this process. Of particular interest is an initial configuration with a double inner horizon coexisting with a simple event horizon. We show that neutral emission necessarily splits the inner root into two simple ones, revealing a horizon fine structure. For charged emission, the dependence of extracted charge on emitted energy determines the separation law and allows that preservation or later restore the degeneracy. We construct such channels connecting the same initial and final states through distinct internal histories sharing the same leading semiclassical factor. As emission continues, the larger of the newly separated inner horizons can coalesce with the event horizon, driving the sequence towards extremality with a vanishing temperature but finite tunneling probability. We find that zero temperature cannot be attained in finite boundary time while uniform adiabaticity bounds hold. We also establish a regime where the geometric expansion and the canonical thermal approximation remain controlled near this endpoint. Finally, applying this analysis to the sector reproducing a quantum-backreacted BTZ geometry reveals how the leading semiclassical corrections raise the temperature and enhance the neutral-probe horizon emission factor relative to classical BTZ.

title: Positivity, Noise, and Cones
summary: As a consequence of causality, Euclidean-time correlation functions in quantum field theory are subject to constraints in the form of positivity conditions on certain Hankel matrices. Such conditions define convex conic structures. Correlation functions computed numerically using Monte Carlo techniques generally contain statistical fluctuations that violate the positivity conditions. This work describes a projection procedure, based on the convex conic geometry induced by the positivity conditions and a statistical covariance matrix, that can be used to restore positivity, providing a unique decomposition for noisy correlators into causal and acausal components. In contrast to previous literature, this work explicitly leverages the conic structure and not just the convex nature of the causal space. The projection can be computed using primal-dual interior-point methods. Constrained projection gives rise to observable-specific frequentist confidence intervals for smeared spectral densities in the causal bootstrap of [Phys. Rev. D 114, 074510 (2026)]. Analytic results are supported with numerical examples.

title: Separable equations of motion for spinning test bodies in spacetimes with Killing--Yano symmetry
summary: At linear order in spin, the motion of a spinning compact body in curved spacetime is known to have two remarkable properties: (i) in Kerr spacetime, a suitable shift of the worldline maps the motion onto fiducial geodesics, yielding separable equations of motion; and (ii) in four-dimensional spacetimes admitting a non-degenerate Killing--Yano tensor, the dynamics are integrable. In this work, we generalize the worldline-shift method of (i) to the whole class of spacetimes in (ii), using a covariant construction built on the Killing--Yano symmetry. We show that spin then plays the role of charge: after the shift, the motion is described by a fictitious spinless particle, with charge set by the spin component along the orbital angular momentum, obeying a Lorentz-force equation. The effective field strength is built from the Ricci tensor and the dual of the Killing--Yano tensor. It vanishes in Ricci-flat spacetimes, recovering the geodesic description known in Kerr. In the general off-shell metric admitting a Killing--Yano tensor, we derive explicitly separated equations of motion, which reduce to quadratures and provide a constructive realization of the known integrability. Since no field equations are assumed, our results apply to any such spacetime, including those sourced by matter or arising in modified theories of gravity, and we illustrate them in Kerr--de Sitter spacetime.

title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: Wave-optics Signatures of Ultralight Fields on Lensed Gravitational Waves
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagate through the universe from sources at high redshift, experiencing the gravitational fields of the intervening matter distribution. Halos composed of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) contain strong density fluctuations, reflecting the interference pattern in the field distribution of the ultralight bosons. In the wave-optics regime, ULDM fluctuations act as a diffractive grating, imprinting frequency-dependent modulations of GWs, in addition to magnification and other gravitational lensing effects. Since lensing depends on the projected surface density, we derive its approximate probability distribution and show how it departs from a Gaussian distribution depending on the halo profile and coherence length. We then quantify how the GW diffraction signatures produced by the granules depend on macroimage magnification and parity. The ULDM interference network imprints stochastic diffraction fluctuations at the $O(1)\%$ level on GWs moderately lensed by the host when the Fresnel scale is comparable to the granule coherence length $r_F(f)\sim\ell_c$. These fluctuations can be enhanced to $\gtrsim10\%$ when the host macroimage forms near the critical curve or for Type II macroimages. For massive black hole binaries observed by LISA, the diffraction signature can be detectable around the ULDM particle mass $m_φ\sim10^{-21}$ eV, providing either a smoking-gun signature of ULDM or new constraints on $m_φ$.

authors: The Broad-Band X-ray Science Analysis Group
title: The Science and Technology of Broad-Band X-ray Astrophysics
comment: BBX-SAG Co-Chairs: Chien-Ting Chen (MSFC), Kristin K. Madsen (GSFC) & Daniel Stern (JPL). A report to the NASA Astrophysics Leadership and the Physics of the Cosmos Program office by the Broad-band X-ray Science Analysis Group https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/community/bbx-sag/
summary:
Much of our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena over the past decade has relied on coordinated observations extending from soft X-rays (<10 keV) to hard X-rays (>10 keV). While soft X-ray facilities remain abundant, focusing capabilities above ~10 keV are scarce, representing the primary gap for broad-band X-ray science. Simultaneous wide-band observations are essential to study thermal and non-thermal processes in extreme environments such as accretion discs, jets, and coronae. However, current high-energy observations remain limited by a lack of high angular resolution and sensitivity beyond Chandra's bandpass. With upcoming multi-messenger facilities set to dramatically increase variable and transient sources, a high angular resolution broad-band X-ray mission is critically needed.
  This report reviews the current landscape of high-energy facilities, outlines key science drivers, focusing on extragalactic accretion (the cosmic X-ray background) and Galactic compact objects, and examines the underlying technology landscape, including optics and detectors. Broad-band X-ray astrophysics is primed to address key questions from the Astro2020 Decadal Survey. While past focusing efforts have been limited to the Small Explorer class, technological advances now enable low-risk Probe- or Flagship-class architectures capable of delivering order-of-magnitude improvements in capabilities.

title: Are AGN Required? Updated Photoionization Models for Rest-UV Line Diagnostics in Reionization-era Galaxies
summary: Rest-frame ultraviolet (UV) emission lines in galaxies provide important probes of the ionizing radiation, chemical abundances, and interstellar medium conditions. Here, we consider UV emission-line diagnostics for galaxies with the observed physical properties of young, metal-poor stellar populations in the epoch of reionization. We study eight $z \sim 7$--$9$ galaxies using deep JWST/NIRSpec G140M and G395M spectroscopy from the Carbon-3 plus Oxygen survey. We measure rest-frame UV and optical emission lines, $\mathrm{C\,IV}$ $λ\lambda1548,1551$, $\mathrm{He\,II}$ $\lambda1640$, $\mathrm{O\,III]}$ $\lambda1666$, $\mathrm{C\,III]}$ $λ\lambda1907,1909$, $\mathrm{[O\,II]}$ $λ\lambda3727,3730$, H$γ$, $\mathrm{[O\,III]}$ $\lambda4364$, H$β$, and $\mathrm{[O\,III]}$ $λ\lambda4960,5008$. The galaxies have low oxygen abundances, $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.50$-$7.90$, low C/O ratios, $\mathrm{C/O}=0.10$-$0.32$, and high electron densities, $n_e(\mathrm{C\,III]})=(1.9-4.9)\times10^4\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$. We compute Cloudy photoionization models using BPASS and BC03 stellar populations to test how lower C/O and higher gas density affect the UV diagnostics. We find that reducing C/O and increasing the gas density shift the star-forming grids into regions conventionally classified as composite or AGN-like. We therefore conclude that positions within these regions alone do not establish the presence of an AGN in the galaxies studied here. However, some lines remain enigmatic, including strong $\mathrm{He\,II}$, which is not reproduced by the updated models. These results highlight the need for UV diagnostic boundaries that account for the abundance patterns and gas conditions of galaxies during the epoch of reionization.

title: Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC
summary: Quantum information observables in top quark pair production have opened a new experimental window on non-classical correlations of particle interactions at colliders. Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering occupies a distinguished place in the quantum hierarchy, lying between entanglement and Bell nonlocality. We present a detailed collider analysis of steerability for top quark pairs at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). In particular, we utilize both the decay and kinematic methods to estimate the expected sensitivity of the LHC and High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to detect steerable states. We find that with the current LHC dataset of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ the steerability of the $t\bar t$ state in the boosted region can be established at $7.7σ$ ($1.8σ$) in the semileptonic (dileptonic) channel with the decay method, corresponding to a measurement of the steerability integral at a precision of $1.5\%$ ($5.2\%$), while the kinematic method reaches a precision of $0.05\%$ in both channels. At the HL-LHC the decay-method precision improves to $0.3\%$ ($1.1\%$). Near threshold, where the inclusive selections used for entanglement and discord yield a state at the steerability boundary, an optimized selection $M_{t\bar{t}}\lesssim360$--$400$~GeV isolates a steerable singlet-dominated state, where the sensitivity is projected to reach $7σ$ ($3.4σ$). We also provide a detailed discussion on the interpretation of these results with respect to fictitious quantum states, and argue for the robust nature of the steerability measurement at colliders.

title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
summary: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

title: Interpretable uncertainties for bounds on spectral functionals from Euclidean correlators
summary: Positivity of the spectral density, combined with a $χ^2$ measure of compatibility with the data, bounds every linear functional of the spectral density of a Euclidean correlator to an interval. We show how such an interval is turned into a central value with statistical and systematic errors that have a definite meaning. We first show that, at typical precision, the best positive fit of noisy data has $χ^2_{\min}>0$, with a probability bounded from below by the distance of the noise-free data from the boundary of the set of data of positive spectra. Numerically, it does not depend on the number of states. The threshold must therefore be set relative to $χ^2_{\min}$. With $Δχ^2=1$, the interval reproduces Gaussian error propagation when positivity does not act, and positivity can only narrow it. We define the statistical error by the jackknife and the systematic error as the remaining, non-Gaussian part of the interval, which becomes a systematic error that does not decrease with the statistics in the high-statistics limit. Coverage tests for correlators and for smeared spectral densities and step functions give nominal coverage for outputs determined by the data and mostly conservative coverage otherwise. The exceptions are effects of the statistical error on the error estimate that disappear as the statistics is increased. Additional bounds on the spectral density, for example from perturbation theory, further reduce the systematic error substantially without loss of coverage. For long-distance correlators the method uses the same information as the bounding method, and its error agrees with that of the bounding method up to the remaining gap between the bounds.

title: Filling the interior of the light cone
summary: The retarded Green's function of gravitational waves in a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker universe contains, besides the light-cone term, a tail supported inside the light cone. We formulate the tail, for homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds, as the solution of a ``\textit{Goursat problem},'' {\emph{i.e.}}, a hyperbolic partial differential equation with boundary conditions given on two intersecting characteristic curves. In this sense, we fill the interior of the light cone. We solve this problem directly in position space for any expansion history, and compare exact solutions in $Λ$CDM independently with a convergent double series about the coincidence point, and with an approximate analytic interaction model. We discuss the interpretation of the tail as the sum of the waves scattered off the background curvature, as suggested by its expansion in powers of the curvature potential. Our novel solutions allow us to follow the tail throughout the entire expansion history, from the electroweak epoch to today. We find that the tail of an early source records the trace of the cosmic fluid along the light cone, ordered in retarded time: single scattering accounts for its features in the radiation era, while multiple scattering is needed in the matter era. This work establishes the accuracy of our calculation of the tail and lays the groundwork for its applications. From the position-space data we obtain the large-$k$ expansion of the propagator. Its first correction, the effect of the tail, depends on the curvature potential integrated along the light cone. The applications of the tail, the power spectrum of a background of bursts, and the memory waveform of a single burst, both of which require convolving the Green's function with its source, are presented in follow-up papers.

title: Inverse Reconstruction of Two-Field Potentials for a DESI-Motivated Phantom-Divide Transition
summary: A phantom-divide transition favored by recent cosmological observations poses an inverse problem: which field potentials realize the inferred expansion history, and what features are uniquely fixed by it? We reconstruct local potentials for a canonical-phantom scalar pair with standard matter and radiation, targeting Metastable Emergent Dark Energy histories constrained by CMB, DESI BAO, and Type Ia supernova data. The coupled-field Friedmann evolution reproduces the target background to numerical accuracy across the transition, with regular perturbations through the crossing. At the phantom divide, the transition slope sets a dimensionless potential-energy release rate insensitive to the partition of kinetic energy. We identify local potential deformations that preserve both background expansion and linear dynamics. This construction gives a classical field realization of the inferred transition and disentangles observationally fixed energy balances from interaction terms requiring additional theoretical input.

title: A higher-order smoothness indicator as refinement criterion for Newtonian and relativistic MHD simulations
summary: Adaptive mesh refinement is a widely adopted strategy for grid-based numerical simulation codes to mitigate the high computational cost of multi-length scale problems. A robust and reliable mesh refinement criterion with minimal requirement for problem-specific tuning is critical for efficient and accurate simulations. Motivated by the oscillation indicators used in the spectral methods literature, we develop a new mesh refinement criterion employing a 5-point stencil for multi-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics simulations, essentially extending the conventional 3-point Löhner scheme. We implement the criterion in the astrophysical fluid dynamics code AthenaK and test it across a variety of benchmark problems in Newtonian, special relativistic, and general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics, demonstrating its robustness and versatility.

title: Orbital parameters for 50 million stars observed by Gaia and spectroscopic surveys
summary: Together with ground-based spectroscopic stellar surveys, the Gaia mission has changed Galactic archaeology over the past decade. Nevertheless, attempts to combine these datasets remain scarce, even though precise orbital parameters for as many stars as possible are crucial to unraveling the Galaxy's formation and evolutionary history. This work aims to construct the largest homogeneous catalog of stellar orbital parameters ever compiled to date, using the most up-to-date data from nine large-scale spectroscopic stellar surveys (Gaia RVS DR3, APOGEE DR19, BOSS DR19, LAMOST DR11, Gaia-ESO DR5, GALAH DR4, RAVE DR6, SEGUE DR12, DESI DR1), combined with Gaia DR3 astrometric data and employing an orbital integration tool for orbital modeling. Our catalog includes orbital parameters, such as orbital distances, eccentricity, inclination, energy, angular momentum, and actions, for 52,423,233 stellar sources from Bailer-Jones distances, and 40,355,569 stellar sources from recomputed StarHorse distances, of which 41,100,866 and 30,777,133 are unique objects, respectively. We also included probabilities of belonging to specific Galactic components based on kinematic classification and chemical-abundance classification. Using this catalog, we recover the known kinematic substructures of the Galactic disk while extending their mapping to Galactocentric distances of $\sim17$ kpc, demonstrating the potential of the combined dataset for studies of Galactic dynamics and evolution. We expect that this catalog will benefit a broad range of research areas, from stellar astrophysics to Galactic archaeology.

title: Why supersonic UAP events are not accompanied by acoustic booms?

title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
summary: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. The modified solution-generating techniques allow one to introduce both the dyonic charges and external electromagnetic fields independently into Ricci-flat seed metrics in both theories, without generating either Taub-NUT or Taub-swirling twists.

title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
summary: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.

title: Thermodynamic Degeneracy and Distinct Horizon Geometries of Rotating Kaluza-Klein Black Holes in Independent External Electric and Magnetic Fields
summary: We construct an exact finite-rotation solution of four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory at the Kaluza-Klein coupling, immersed in independent external electric and magnetic fields. Exact algebraic balance identities reveal two distinct regular nonextremal branches with identical horizon area, quasi-local angular momentum, and electromagnetic fluxes. Under a common, explicitly specified reference prescription for the axial clock, rotational frame, and electromagnetic potentials, the two branches also have identical thermodynamic readouts, including energy, temperature, angular velocity, and electric and magnetic potentials. Nevertheless, the two branches possess nonisometric intrinsic horizon geometries, with every positive axisymmetric scalar-Laplacian eigenvalue strictly ordered between them. Thus, identical thermodynamic readouts do not uniquely determine the intrinsic geometry of a black hole horizon. We further establish that the exterior admits consistent asymptotic matching to two distinct exact rotating cylindrical backgrounds associated with its northern and southern polar regions. Their metric, dilaton, and electromagnetic fields become compatible in the angular overlap region, with uniform matching extending to both symmetry axes. Every regular noncritical exterior, including the supercritical branches, is globally hyperbolic.

title: Reconstructing the mass-redshift distribution of supermassive black holes using multiband gravitational-wave observations
summary: The formation and evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in astrophysics. Astrophysical models of SMBHs invoke black-hole (BH) seeds formed at high redshift, which subsequently grow through gas accretion and mergers. Although observations of high-redshift quasars and active galactic nuclei constrain these scenarios, the mechanisms governing SMBH formation and growth remain uncertain. Future gravitational-wave (GW) observations across the millihertz, decihertz, and audio-frequency bands will provide a complementary and direct probe of SMBH assembly by tracing their merger history. We investigate the extent to which multiband GW observations can reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers. We simulate populations of BH mergers predicted by different astrophysical models and identify those observable by the millihertz detector LISA, the decihertz detector LGWA, and next-generation ground-based detectors operating in the audio-frequency band. We reconstruct the mass-redshift distribution of these mergers using the nonparametric inference code FIGARO. We find that combining observations across frequency bands substantially improves the reconstruction for the light-seed models considered here, whose merger populations span broad ranges of mass and redshift. In contrast, for the heavy-seed models considered here, LISA alone recovers most of the accessible mass-redshift distribution, with little additional improvement from the multiband network.

title: Redrock: Spectroscopic Classification and Redshift Fitting for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
summary: Redrock is a software package for spectroscopic classification and redshift fitting, designed to use the full information from spectroperfectionism outputs: flux-calibrated spectra, uncorrelated errors, and a per-spectrum resolution matrix encoding the non-Gaussian wavelength-dependent spectral line-spread function. Redrock was originally developed for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), but the Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS) also used Redrock as their primary galaxy redshift fitter prior to DESI. This paper presents the algorithmic details of Redrock and its performance on DESI data. On spectra from DESI DR2, Redrock achieves a redshift recovery rate of approximately 98% for the Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) and Luminous Red Galaxies (LRG), 95.9% for Emission Line Galaxies (ELG), and 92.6% for quasars (QSO), and it delivers unbiased stellar radial velocities with a precision of roughly 5 km/s.

title: Excess intergalactic heating around a dual quasar system 2.8 Gyr after the Big Bang
comment: 17 pages, 12 figures, Published online in Nature Astronomy on 18 Nov 2026
summary: Galaxy formation models necessitate that actively growing supermassive black holes, or quasars, strongly impact their environments. Theory suggests that quasar winds produce very hot gas bubbles that extend through the host galaxy and into the circumgalactic medium. Because this gas component is so hot and diffuse, the only way to measure its total energy is through the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect. Here we report the discovery of a dual quasar system at z=2.37 which is embedded in a bubble of hot gas as detected (at 6 $σ$) by a tSZ flux decrement at millimeter wavelengths. The total thermal energy of the hot gas is 9.7 x 10$^{60}$ erg. This energy exceeds the amount expected from all of the hot gas in a 10$^{13}$ M$_\odot$ dark matter halo by a factor of 3.6, and constitutes at least 0.6% of the quasar's lifetime energy output. We also find evidence for hot gas on larger (100-600 kpc) scales that may also originate in quasar outflows. This considerable excess energy is more than sufficient to shut off star formation and heat the intergalactic medium, implying a significant impact from quasar-driven winds on their surroundings. Such feedback plausibly explains the steep decline of the bright end of the luminosity function of galaxies across the observable Universe, and thus provides evidence to further support leading galaxy evolution theory.

title: The Price of Discovery: Cost-Optimized Detectors for the GUT-Scale QCD Axion
comment: 45 pages, 13 figures, code at https://github.com/bsafdi/axionMultiPhysics, video abstract at https://youtu.be/h7Q-nishtLs
summary: Grand unification and string theory point to a quantum chromodynamics (QCD) axion with mass between $10^{-11}$ and $10^{-8}$ eV, while heterotic string theory suggests a mass of $0.5-0.8$ neV. If projected readout targets are met, a 5 m toroid at 25 MCHF suffices. We find these designs by optimizing the toroid, solenoid, and core lumped-element topologies under a common cost metric. The toroid emerges as the most promising and cost-effective topology. The optimal field of the toroid detector is far below the 16 T of the proposed DMRadio-GUT design, which would cost nearly twice as much as our optimum. Heterodyne searches with superconducting radio-frequency cavities, with cavity shapes that we optimize for price, cost between about the same as and twice as much as the lumped-element detectors, but require cavities of volumes $\sim50-2000$ m$^3$. We find that nuclear-magnetic-resonance searches (CASPEr) need orders-of-magnitude gains in spin polarization and coherence. We release axionMultiPhysics, an open-source finite-element and multiphysics package for, e.g., magnetoquasistatic and full-wave electromagnetics, superconductors, readout circuits, and mechanics, from which most of our numerical results were obtained.

title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
summary: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
summary: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

title: Dynamics of a spinning body with scalar multipoles
summary: We construct an effective worldline action for a spinning compact object in theories of gravity with massless, non-minimally coupled scalar fields. title: Computation of complex dust grain optical properties: Optimisation method by equivalent representation (OMER)

title: JEPA for astronomy: multi-survey spectral alignment puts stellar parameters on the leading principal axes
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AAS journals. Comments welcome
summary: Spectra from different surveys carry different systematics and are not calibrated against one another. title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes

We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH. Consequently, the 211 cloud mass is bounded from above by M_{211}^{crit}/M~=5*10^{-3}*alpha^{-1/2}*[f_a/10^{16} GeV]^2 up to an O(1) factor depending on the spin of the BH. Crucially, for rapidly spinning BHs with M~<4*10^6 M_{sun}, alpha~<0.03, and f_a~<9*10^{15} GeV the resulting superradiant cloud mass is lower than previously assumed, which might have an impact on axion bounds from measurements of stellar BH spins.

title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
summary: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar. In all cases we compare $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ as computed in a truncated low-energy effective theory by an appropriate integral over constrained wormholes. In each case we find that, even though $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ are related by an integral transform, the two generally receive contributions from differing sets of saddles. Along the way, we uncover a variety of additional interesting subtleties associated with semiclassical contributions to our $Z_D$ and $Z_N$.

title: Total Angular Momentum Assignments in the Hadron Spectrum
summary: Predicting the total angular momentum $J$ for hadronic resonances whose spins have not yet been experimentally determined constitutes an important step in the spectroscopy of observed hadrons. In the present study, we develop a data-driven model in order to predict the value of $ J $ for hadrons with unknown spins using a dataset of known mesons and baryons from the PDG, including information on their quark content, isospin, parity, mass and other spectroscopic features. In particular, we employ XGBoost classifiers along with nested optimization in order to discover spectroscopic patterns across different hadronic sectors. We also prepare a systematic list of hadrons with unknown or poorly determined values of $ J $, and study spin-parity assignments for those hadrons. Since the parity hypothesis is taken as an input to the model, our model predicts the value of $ J $ conditional on a given parity hypothesis rather than independently determining the full $J^P$ assignment. Our predictions for several theoretically studied states show good agreement with results from quark models, QCD sum rules, molecular models, and other phenomenological approaches, while predictions for some other states differ from existing theoretical assignments. These differences motivate further theoretical investigations and may be tested by future experimental measurements.

title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
comment: 2 pages. Includes supplemental material. Comment on arXiv:2511.14047
summary: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.

title: Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions with Full Nonlinear Gravity
summary: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can contribute to the stochastic gravitational wave background. For decades, these first-order phase transitions have been studied using a Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background where the gravitational waves are treated as linear perturbations. We simulate a universe that contains a scalar field alongside a relativistic radiation fluid. We focus on GUT-scale transitions in which bubbles nucleate near the horizon size. We describe a method to construct initial data that satisfies the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints, starting from a Coleman--de~Luccia-like bubble profile and adjusting the bubble radius. We compute the gravitational wave spectrum directly from the trace-free extrinsic curvature and find a present-day peak amplitude of $Ω_{\rm GW,0}h^2 \sim 5\times 10^{-11}$, consistent with earlier results that do not include nonlinear gravity. The peak frequency depends on the symmetry-breaking scale and could fall anywhere from the LISA band to GHz frequencies. At late times, the field fragments into long-lived oscillons, which push its effective equation of state toward that of matter.

title: Stars and gas in the most metal-poor galaxies -- II. Search for VMS and determination of stellar population and nebular properties at $Z\lesssim0.1\,Z_\odot$
summary:
Constraining the properties of OB-star populations and ionized gas at low metallicity is essential for understanding a broad range of astrophysical objects, from stellar black holes to the first galaxies. Rest-frame UV spectra of nearby metal-poor galaxies provide crucial constraints on theoretical predictions of low-metallicity stars and gas. However, such spectra are scarce at $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, and candidate Very Massive Stars (VMS) remain elusive.
  We analyse optical and new UV spectra of nearby star-forming galaxies with $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, selected for their nebular He II $\lambda4686$ emission and lack of Wolf-Rayet blue and red bumps, making them promising targets for VMS searches. Some galaxies exhibit stellar wind features (group 1), while others do not (group 2). For group 1, we compare STARBURST99, GALAXEV, and BPASS predictions with observed stellar lines to constrain OB-population ages and masses. The inferred ages are too old for VMS to be present. We also use pySTARBURST99 and GALAXEV photoionization models to investigate the ionized gas in a subsample, finding no evidence for VMS-dominated ionization.
  The absence of detected VMS may reflect their rarity, our limited sample size, or shortcomings in current models. Moreover, reproducing the extreme optical and UV line ratios simultaneously requires unrealistic N/O, ionization parameters, or Lyman continuum escape fractions, suggesting that multiple ionizing-source populations may be needed.

title: Leading Axion Sensitivity with Interstellar Medium Optical Line Emission
summary: We introduce interstellar optical line emission as a new probe of axion dark matter. Axion decays to photons or electrons can excite or ionize neutral hydrogen, producing H$α$ emission at a fixed atomic wavelength rather than at an energy set by the axion mass. Developing the formalism and applying it to the Leo T galaxy with Very Large Telescope data, we derive strong constraints for eV--GeV scale axions, covering new regions of parameter space for both axion-photon and axion-electron couplings. These results establish optical line measurements as a new discovery channel for axion dark matter, probe poorly constrained parameter space below hydrogen's ionization threshold, and constrain axion explanations of JWST's high-redshift supermassive-black-hole observations.

title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}. Thus we construct the perturbation theory on these backgrounds in addition to exploring ER=EPR when $G_{N}=0$, in the limit it is perturbatively small and beyond perturbation theory.

title: Helicity-squared scaling of post-eikonal phases for electromagnetic and gravitational waves in Ricci-flat spacetimes
summary: Spin-optical descriptions of electromagnetic and gravitational waves isolate finite-frequency corrections that are odd in the helicity. We study the complementary, helicity-even part of the first post-eikonal correction for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational waves on Ricci-flat backgrounds. In a parallel-propagated null tetrad, the direct Weyl coupling of the gravitational field projects onto the circular transverse-traceless states as the multiple $2C_{\bar m m\bar m m}$ of the identity. The Ricci identity for the spin coefficient $μ$ then rewrites this projection as a total derivative plus optical terms. The helicity-even phase of a spin-$s$ wave, measured relative to the scalar wave, then obeys a helicity-squared law, $Δ_2=4Δ_1$, up to endpoint terms. The Weyl coupling is what completes the $h^2$ scaling in the gravitational case. For weak-deflection scattering by a Schwarzschild black hole we evaluate the relevant integrals along the ray and obtain $Δ_s=-3πs^2/(8Mωρ^3)$, with $ρ=b/M$. The same coefficient follows independently, and without reference to any frame or gauge, from the Regge--Wheeler phase shifts combined with the asymptotics of the rotation functions $d^l_{ss}$. Direct numerical integration of the radial equations confirms it. At first order in $M$ the helicity-even phase difference vanishes, as required by the Born amplitudes. The helicity-odd spin-optical sector and the helicity-even post-eikonal sector are therefore organized by the first and second powers of the helicity, respectively.

title: Stratonovich approximation for halo bias: An efficient framework within excursion set theory
summary: We develop an efficient framework for calculating halo multiplicity functions and bias parameters in the excursion-set approach based on the previously presented Hertz and Stratonovich approximations for the first-crossing distribution. The framework enables efficient evaluation of first-crossing distributions for a broad class of moving barriers and filter functions, from which halo biases can be calculated within the peak-background split formalism. We compare halo multiplicity functions and biases obtained from these approximations with those computed from first-crossing distributions obtained from numerically generated ensembles of excursion-set trajectories. We find close agreement between predictions based on the Stratonovich approximation and numerical results across a range of barrier parameters and filter choices, demonstrating that the approximation captures the impact of non-Markovian correlations on first-crossing statistics while substantially reducing the computational cost compared to trajectory-based calculations. Overall, this framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for analyzing halo statistics in cosmological applications.

title: Zippers and Twisters II: The lopsidedness of satellite systems around local massive galaxies emerges from a shifting cosmic web landscape

The NewHorizon sample is generally skewed towards being more lopsided than naive expectations. This cautions against using dark matter or under-resolved hydrodynamic simulations as a null-hypothesis to compare to real systems. We find broad, hemispheric lopsidedness to be much more prevalent than narrow lopsidedness inherited from group infall. Across all systems, the dividing plane between the richest and emptiest hemispheres is systematically aligned with a nearby intermediate-scale cosmic filament. Further analysis reveals that the lopsidedness of systems is largely inherited from that of the network of filaments feeding them. The most populated side almost systematically contains the highest number of filaments. Such anisotropies of local filament networks are often indicative of on-going or recent zippers (filament merger $<2$ Gyr). Converging filamentary structures therefore funnel satellites preferentially onto one side of host halos, naturally generating lopsided configurations without requiring galaxy mergers. Twister remnants (of high orbital momentum mergers of filaments) are also found on the richest hemisphere of our systems, perhaps reminiscent of vorticity preventing mergers hence causing satellites' pooling. These results suggest that lopsidedness is primarily an outcome of the evolution of the intermediate-scale cosmic web. This highlights the need for increased hydrodynamic resolution in simulations.

title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
summary: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. Supported by numerical evaluations, this framework establishes OPEC and OPCC angular widths as sensitive probes of higher-twist dynamics and fundamental properties of cold nuclear matter.

title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
summary: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($β=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $λ$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $β_f$ playing the role of $β$. We demonstrate both numerically and analytically that the resulting folded OTOC displays anti-scrambling. The exact DSSYK evaluation tracks the semiclassical de Sitter eikonal formula in the scrambling regime, including a time advance instead of a time delay.The direction of the fold selects the side from which the continued eikonal amplitude approaches its branch cut. We show how our results are consistent with recent ``no-go" constraints. We compare the folded correlator with the two-shell analysis of arXiv:2607.14215: the growing term of the two-shell dilaton invariant appears in DSSYK with the same exponent, but as an imaginary part, while its real part, which would signal the backreaction that ends in a crunch, only moves by $O(λ)$ for thermal-scale probes. We also generalize to finite $β$; we find reasonable agreement with the de Sitter eikonal form for sufficiently high temperatures, but at lower temperatures the folded correlator is dominated by a pair of complex conjugate saddles, an anti-Stokes crossover that prevents retrieval of the eikonal behavior from the folded OTOC.

title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
summary: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $η\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $α\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $λ\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

title: Towards modelling redshift uncertainties in the photometric void size function
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for submission to ApJL
summary: We present an extension of the theoretical formalism for the Void Size Function (VSF) to incorporate photometric redshift uncertainties, combining the excursion set with the theory of Lagrangian density peaks. Photometric redshift scatter induces anisotropic line-of-sight smoothing of the density field, which modifies the variance of the field and suppresses the abundance of large voids. We model this effect by damping the variance of the smoothed density field in the theoretical model, and we test it on AbacusSummit halo lightcones with true redshifts and with mock photometric redshifts generated with a Gaussian scatter. The predicted damping of the variance agrees with the one measured in the halo distribution to 1% and the suppression of the VSF due to photometric redshift scatter is well reproduced by the modified model, with recalibrated barrier parameters, for sigma_z <= 0.015 and for voids larger than 40 Mpc/h (about 2.5 mean tracer separations). This work is a first step towards modelling the VSF in modern photometric surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time and the Euclid mission.
